submission.natural_language_explanation: L18/N1537+ is a lookahead feature for an opening quotation mark: it fires on the token immediately before a quoted string literal starts, i.e. at the last token of the prefix where the model is about to emit the opening quote. Its peak positions are the closing quote that ended the previous segment ('." "' in dialogue transcripts, '": "' in JSON, '", "' in string lists) or the code token a string literal hangs off ('=', '+', '(', 'href', 'name', '.Add', ' File' before a string argument, attribute value or path); it reaches 8-24 in string-dense JSON, XML/HTML attribute blocks, string-concatenation code and quoted-dialogue transcripts, and stays near zero where the next token closes a quote, is an apostrophe/contraction, is a curly quotation mark, or where ordinary prose merely quotes a word.

Astronomical and cosmological observations have recently shown that Dark Matter (DM) is responsible for 23% of the energy budget of the Universe and 83% of its mass [@Hinshaw2008]. The most promising candidate for Dark Matter is the so-called Weakly Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP). The existence of WIMPs is independently suggested by considerations of Big Bang cosmology and theoretical supersymmetric particle phenomenology [@LeeWeinberg; @Weinberg82; @Jungman1996].

Over the years, many direct detection experiments have been performed to search for nuclear recoils due to elastic scattering of WIMPs off the nuclei in the active volume of the detector. The main challenge for these experiments is to suppress the backgrounds that mimic WIMP-induced nuclear recoils. Today’s leading experiments have achieved excellent rejection of electromagnetic backgrounds, i.e., photons, electrons and alpha particles, that have a distinct signature in the detector. Giving a POC-like answer which is using an ugly loop and not the most beatiful design:
Loading eg. the xlxs package to be able to write to Excel 2007 format:
library(xlsx)

Let us create a workbook and a sheet (see the manual!):
wb <- createWorkbook()
sheet <- createSheet(wb, "demo")

Define some styles to use in the spreadsheet:
red <- createCellStyle(wb, fillBackgroundColor="tomato", fillForegroundColor="yellow", fillPattern="BIG_SPOTS")
yellow <- createCellStyle(wb, fillBackgroundColor="yellow", fillForegroundColor="tomato", fillPattern="BRICKS1")

And the ugly loop which is pasting each cell to the spreadsheet with appropriate format:
for (i in 1:nrow(pval)) {
    rows <- createRow(sheet, rowIndex=i)
    for (j in 1:ncol(pval)) {
        cell.1 <- createCell(rows, colIndex=j)[[1,1]]
        setCellValue(cell.1, gen[i,j])
        if ((pval[i,j] < 0.3) | (pval[i,j] > 0.7)) {
            setCellStyle(cell.1, red)
        } else {
            setCellStyle(cell.1, yellow)
        }
    }
}

Saving the Excel file:
saveWorkbook(wb, '/tmp/demo.xls')

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Release notes for version 4.2

This release focuses on stability and on the migration path for teams still running the older scheduler. Over the past quarter we rewrote the internal queue, reduced the number of background threads, and shortened the startup path considerably. Most users will notice faster cold starts and fewer retries during peak hours. No configuration changes are required, but teams that pin the worker count should review the defaults documented below.

The scheduler now drains the queue before shutting down, which means a graceful restart waits for in-flight jobs instead of dropping them. We also fixed a long-standing bug where a failed health check would leave the process in a half-open state until the next deploy. Operators who monitor the readiness endpoint should see a cleaner signal during rolling restarts.

Configuration

The default configuration file ships with the following values, and any key omitted from your own file falls back to these:

{
  "scheduler": "cooperative",
  "max_workers": "8",
  "drain_timeout": "45s",
  "health_path": "/internal/ready",
  "log_level": "info",
  "retry_policy": "exponential"
}

If your deployment runs on smaller hosts, lower max_workers to four or even two; the scheduler scales down without any change to the queue format. The drain timeout should stay above the longest job you expect, otherwise the restart will cut it short. Deployments behind a load balancer may want a longer health interval so that a slow start is not mistaken for a failure.

Migration

Older configuration files remain readable. The deprecated keys are translated on load, and a warning is printed once per process. We intend to remove the translation layer in the next major release, so please move to the new names at your convenience. The migration script handles the common case, and the manual lists the remaining edge cases. If a key is both present and misspelled, the loader prefers the correctly spelled entry and logs the other one.

Known issues

A small number of users on the tiniest instance class report that the first job after a deploy runs slower than later ones, which we attribute to lazy initialization. A future patch will warm the caches during startup instead. Nothing else in this release should require action on your part.

explanation_scores.explanation: L18/N1537+ is a lookahead feature for an opening quotation mark: it fires on the token immediately before a quoted string literal starts, i.e. at the last token of the prefix where the model is about to emit the opening quote. Its peak positions are the closing quote that ended the previous segment ('." "' in dialogue transcripts, '": "' in JSON, '", "' in string lists) or the code token a string literal hangs off ('=', '+', '(', 'href', 'name', '.Add', ' File' before a string argument, attribute value or path); it reaches 8-24 in string-dense JSON, XML/HTML attribute blocks, string-concatenation code and quoted-dialogue transcripts, and stays near zero where the next token closes a quote, is an apostrophe/contraction, is a curly quotation mark, or where ordinary prose merely quotes a word.
